I have been writing this blog since 2015. Over the years, I’ve written a lot about technology, business, and life, always from the perspective of a software engineer trying to grow, keep learning, and become more professional.

When I read some of my early posts now, they seem almost funny to me. Naive, simple, and sometimes overly confident.

I belong to a generation of coders who used the Internet to learn and ask questions. I benefited enormously from the golden age of <a href="https://stackoverflow.com/" target="_blank">Stack Overflow</a>. I experienced the rise of <a href="https://agilemanifesto.org/" target="_blank">Agile</a>, embraced many of its ideas, and tried to contribute something back to the community through my own writing.

I spent countless hours reading never-ending blog posts about “how to do this with that technology,” usually while trying to solve some problem that had kept me stuck for days.

And now, like everyone else, I’m trying to keep up with a new era: AI coding agents. Always improving, always learning.

It's been a long time since I wrote my last post, and that is not because I have run out of ideas or things to talk about. I am simply starting to wonder whether there is still a point.
I definitely don't see much value anymore in the classic blog post explaining how to do something or how to understand a new technology. A short conversation with a regular AI model can now give you exactly the insight you need, often faster and more directly.

But I have always written, and I don't want to stop. <a href="https://www.joantolos.com/blog/writing-will-make-you-a-better-programmer" target="_blank">I always though of writing as a super power</a>. I just can't stop. So I see two possible directions:
- Write about these new AI technologies and, more specifically, how I am applying them in my day-to-day work.
- Go in a more personal direction and explore the business side of the job: the decisions, trade-offs, communication, leadership, and everything that happens around the code.

So, this is me doing exactly that, my message in a bottle.

I’m still here, still learning, and still trying to improve. I’m completely fascinated by the direction the field is taking, and eager to master these new ways of creating software and delivering value.

I’ve always been an optimist by nature, and I genuinely believe these new tools are going to make our craft even more enjoyable. Not because they make the work disappear, but because they give us new ways to think, create, experiment, and focus on the parts that matter most.
